title: Gullwing Payments introductory call
contextText: Intro call with Gullwing Payments, no recording — notes typed during the call.

note.body:
# Gullwing Payments introductory call

**Date:** February 19
**Attendees:** Alex Rivera (Larkspur Labs), Felix Amundsen (Gullwing Payments), Wen Zhao (Gullwing Payments)

## Summary

First conversation with Gullwing Payments about automating how they handle card chargebacks. Felix Amundsen is Gullwing's CFO and the budget holder. Wen Zhao is a risk analyst on his team who reviews disputes day to day and will be our main working contact.

## Context from Gullwing

- Gullwing processes around 1.2 million chargebacks a year, and the volume has grown every quarter since they entered the travel sector.
- Almost all of the review work is manual today. Wen's team triages each dispute by reading the merchant evidence and the reason code.
- Felix wants a chargeback automation project that pays for itself within a year. He was explicit that he will not fund an open-ended build.
- Wen reports to Felix directly; the risk team is small and stretched.

## Decisions

- Gullwing decided to start with a **paid discovery phase** of four weeks rather than committing to a full build. Felix said he wants numbers before he signs anything bigger.
- Discovery will use a sample of last year's disputes rather than live traffic.

## Action items

- **Alex Rivera** — send two case studies on similar automation work by Monday.
- **Wen Zhao** — pull a sample of last year's disputes, with personal data removed, for the discovery phase.
- **Felix Amundsen** — confirm the discovery budget internally before the end of the month.

## Personal notes

- Wen mentioned she is a keen birdwatcher and spends most weekends at the estuary reserves outside the city. Good small-talk topic.
- Felix prefers short, numbers-first summaries.

## Next steps

Once the budget is confirmed, we schedule a discovery kickoff with Wen's team and agree the sample size. Hana should be looped in on the commercial side.
